result.title: On the Few-Shot Adaptation of Vision-Language Models: A Few Gradient Signs Are All You Need
result.summary: The limited supervision available for the few-shot adaptation of vision-language models makes gradient estimation particularly noisy. We find that the gradient magnitudes are severely miscalibrated, while the signs of a small top-magnitude subset remain informative. This motivates SignSparseSGD and DynSignSparseSGD, two state-free optimizers that use gradient magnitudes only to select where to update and fixed-magnitude signs to decide how to update. The static variant fixes the support after the first minibatch. The dynamic variant refreshes it at every step. Across 11 datasets, three CLIP backbones, and five shot levels, the proposed methods are competitive with or outperform parameter-efficient and optimization-based baselines on average, while exhibiting markedly lower sensitivity to long training schedules. They introduce no task-specific modules, maintain no first- or second-moment optimizer states, and use one shared configuration across datasets, backbones, and shot levels. Our code is included in the supplementary materials and will be released upon publication.

AI.brief_summary: 论文针对视觉-语言模型少样本适配中梯度估计噪声大的问题，发现梯度幅值严重失准但少数大幅值分量的符号仍有信息量，据此提出 SignSparseSGD 与 DynSignSparseSGD：仅用幅值选取更新位置、用固定幅值符号决定更新方向，不保留优化器动量状态，并在 11 个数据集、3 个 CLIP 骨干上验证。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「低监督下梯度噪声大、仅信任稀疏符号方向、免优化器状态」的训练线索，可能可供核查于 latent 推理轨迹训练中的噪声归因与显存受限场景；但论文本身面向分类适配，与视觉证据使用和推理期状态生成无直接关系。
